messages.author: 3d0e230fded30495
messages.subject: Help with my analyses
parts:
Dear all,

I have two samples from two locations. There are five males in my first sample, and only three males in second sample (and around 40 females in each sample). I am not sure if I could even explore male and female shape differences? Preliminary analysis done only on females show homogeneity of allometric slopes, which should allow me to explore allometry-free shape differences between females from two populations. I can't prove common-allometry model for males and females, and visual inspection indicates that they are probably heterogeneous. So, what are my options? Is PCA analysis the most I can do in terms of presenting sexual dimorphism and I should do the rest of my analyses only on females? Maybe I could also plot allometry?

Thanks,
Ellen

messages.author: d6b47e6230fc8cc1
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Re: Help with my analyses
parts:
Dear Ellen,

I think you answered your own question 🙂 In any statistical design one needs to consider the limitations imposed by restricted sampling.  Your case does not lend itself to certain questions (e.g., do male and female shapes varies between populations). You can still retain your male observations and graphically explore differences as an initial foray using deformation grids and (yes) a PCA, with the cavate that you don't have sufficient statistical power to test for significance.

All the best,
Mohamad
